subject: RFI: Sidecar networking, tenant isolation, and egress controls
messages:
From: Ariela Kline <ariela.kline@hawthorne.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@hawthorne.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: network isolation / sidecar model questions

Rishi — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is collecting security clarifications for the platform team. Attached is our RFI (hawthorne-rfi-v1.pdf). Two immediate asks we need clarified before the next vendor round:

1) We run multi-tenant workloads with strict egress controls. Can you describe how Redwood isolates tenant network egress and whether we can pin egress to customer-managed NATs?
2) We use a sidecar proxy pattern for inspection in our infra. Does Redwood support deploying a customer-provided sidecar for traffic inspection between runtime and external services?

Can you please respond by EOD Friday? Attach any diagrams and list any known limitations.

Thanks,
Ariela Kline
Security Engineering Manager
Hawthorne Financial

Attachments: hawthorne-rfi-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Ariela Kline <ariela.kline@hawthorne.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: network isolation / sidecar model questions

Ariela — got it, thanks for the RFI. Looping in Kar (solutions) and Monica (security) to draft a concise response and diagram. We can meet briefly tomorrow if you want to walk through live.

Quick answers up front:
- Egress: Redwood Private supports customer-managed egress (VPC NAT) and per-tenant egress routes; we can document options.
- Sidecars: We do not run arbitrary customer sidecars inside our hosted runtime, but Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) support sidecar patterns via a sidecar bridge or ingress/egress proxies that the customer manages.

Will follow with an attached diagram and a short matrix of supported/unsupported patterns.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0189

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: network isolation / sidecar model questions

Team — I drafted the technical summary and a diagram (see network-sidecar-diagram-20270204.png). Key points I put in the answers spreadsheet:

- Deployment modes: Hosted (no customer-sidecars), Dedicated (managed by Redwood, can configure per-tenant egress rules), Private (customer-controlled VPC/on-prem where sidecars can be orchestrated by the customer).
- Egress options: (1) Redwood-managed NAT (default, shared but segregated by logical rules), (2) Customer NAT/GW via VPC peering (recommended for regulated customers), (3) Explicit per-tenant egress IPs for allowlisting where required.
- Sidecar support: On Private deployments we provide a sidecar bridge pattern — the runtime exposes internal service endpoints on a loopback interface and customers run their inspection proxy in the same VPC. For Dedicated we can run a vetted partner proxy as a managed appliance but cannot run arbitrary third-party processes in our multi-tenant hosted plane.
- Threat considerations: KV-cache leakage is mitigated by per-tenant cache sharding and mandatory token scoping; egress metadata and request tracing are logged to an auditable stream.

Monica — please review the threat bullets and add anything from compliance perspective. Ariela — let me know if you need the diagram in PNG + SVG. I included short stubs for attachments in the sheet.

Attachments: network-sidecar-diagram-20270204.png (image/png)
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: network isolation / sidecar model questions

Thanks Kar — I've added a threat-model summary and controls checklist into the answers workbook (rfi-response-answers-DF4892.xlsx). Highlights to surface to Hawthorne:

- Isolation model: Logical tenant separation enforced at the runtime and network layers; Dedicated/Private allow stronger L2/L3 separation. Access tokens are project-scoped and keys are rotary with RBAC enforced via our control plane.
- Egress assurance: For Private we support customer NAT and HSM-backed customer KMS for keying; for Dedicated we offer egress IP pinning and VPC route controls as part of the reserved capacity contract.
- Sidecar/inspection guidance: Recommend customers run inspection in their VPC and use the sidecar bridge – we provide a validated sample startup manifest and health-check endpoints. Do not expose plaintext logs or model weights to external inspection proxies; use TLS in between and mTLS for control plane hooks.
- Known limitation: Hosted shared plane cannot host customer-managed sidecars; customers who require in-path inspection will need Private or Dedicated with a validated partner proxy.

I'll polish the language and send to Rishi for external. Also added a short runbook entry for audit log exports and request-IDs.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI: network isolation / sidecar model questions

Ariela — thanks for the patience. Attached is our consolidated RFI response (rfi-response-answers-DF4892.xlsx) and a diagram illustrating the sidecar bridge and egress options (network-sidecar-diagram-20270204.png). Summary below: 

1) Egress controls (short):
- Private: full customer-managed egress via VPC NAT/GW; supports HSM-backed KMS and per-tenant egress IPs.
- Dedicated: configurable egress IP pinning and route controls; contractual SLAs for throughput.
- Hosted: Redwood-managed NAT with logical segregation; not suitable for allowlist-only deployments unless paired with Dedicated/Private.

2) Sidecar inspection (short):
- Private: supported. Customers run their sidecar proxy in the same VPC and we provide a sidecar bridge pattern and validated manifests.
- Dedicated: supported via vetted partner proxies; we can collaborate on on-boarding.
- Hosted: unsupported (we do not run customer processes inside the shared runtime).

3) Threat & mitigations (short):
- KV cache isolation via per-tenant sharding + token scoping.
- Egress observability via request tracing and secure audit exports.
- Runtime hardening: kernel and container immutability, restricted syscall surface for inference workers.

Next steps: please confirm whether Hawthorne prefers customer-managed NAT (Private) or egress IP pinning (Dedicated). If helpful, we can set a 30-minute walkthrough next week to go over the diagram and any DocuSign steps for the Dedicated addendum.
